items.text: 医生说这种药必须（ ）吃，一天三次。
items.explain: 按时 (“on time, at the set times”) is an adverb before the verb 吃; with “一天三次” it means taking the medicine at fixed times. 仔细 (“careful”) would not suit a dosing schedule.

items.text: 这篇文章我看了三遍，没想到里面（ ）还有这么多错字。
items.explain: 竟然 (“unexpectedly”) shows surprise, matching “没想到…还有这么多错字”: after reading three times, there were still many typos. It sits before the verb 还有.

items.text: 考试的时候一定要（ ）检查，别因为粗心丢分。
items.explain: 仔细 (“careful, thorough”) is an adverb before 检查; it fits “别因为粗心丢分” (don't lose points through carelessness). 按时 only concerns timing.

items.text: 天气预报说明天降温，出门最好穿（ ）一点儿的衣服。
items.explain: 厚 (“thick”) describes clothes: “穿厚一点儿的衣服” for the cold when the temperature drops. The pattern is adjective + 一点儿 + 的 + noun.

items.text: 对不起，是我误会你了，请你（ ）我。
items.explain: 原谅 (“to forgive”) is a verb with 我 as its object, and it follows the apology “对不起，是我误会你了”. 普遍 (“widespread”) has no meaning here.

items.text:
A：你去超市吗？（ ）帮我买一瓶牛奶吧。
B：没问题，还要别的吗？
items.explain: 顺便 (“while you're at it”) marks an extra errand done on the way: you're going to the shop anyway, so “顺便帮我买…”. 暂时 (“temporarily”) has no such sense.

items.text:
A：这本小说怎么样？
B：非常精彩，很（ ）一读。
items.explain: 值得 (“worth”) forms the pattern “值得 + verb”: “值得一读” means worth reading. The reply “非常精彩” (very exciting) supports it.

items.text:
A：听说小王下个月要去国外读硕士了。
B：真让人（ ），我也想出国看看。
items.explain: 羡慕 (“to envy, admire”) fits “真让人羡慕”: going abroad for a master's is something the speaker also wants (“我也想出国”).

items.text:
A：你的新手机呢？
B：送去修理了，这几天（ ）用我妈的旧手机。
items.explain: 暂时 (“temporarily, for now”) fits because the phone is being repaired for “这几天” only, so the mother's old phone is a short-term substitute.

items.text:
A：你选这家公司的原因是什么？
B：首先是离家近，（ ）是同事们都很友好。
items.explain: 其次 (“secondly”) answers the earlier “首先” (first): 首先 gives the first reason (close to home), 其次 the second (friendly colleagues).

items.text: 这家博物馆不（ ）游客在里面吃东西。
items.explain: 允许 (“to allow”) takes a person plus a verb: “不允许游客…吃东西” means visitors are not allowed to eat. 提醒 (“remind”) would not express a rule.

items.text: 这个办法的（ ）很好，我们的问题很快就解决了。
items.explain: 效果 (“effect, result”) is the noun that fits “这个办法的效果很好”; “问题很快就解决了” shows the method worked well. 印象 (“impression”) does not go with a method.

items.text: 第一次见面，他就给我留下了很深的（ ）。
items.explain: 印象 (“impression”) forms the fixed phrase “留下…印象”; “很深的印象” means a deep impression, after a first meeting.

items.text: 今天的（ ）比昨天低了五度，大家要注意保暖。
items.explain: 温度 (“temperature”) fits “比昨天低了五度” (five degrees lower than yesterday); only temperature can be measured in 度 here.

items.text: 手机上的日历会（ ）我每天按时吃药。
items.explain: 提醒 (“to remind”) is a verb: the calendar on the phone reminds me (我) to take medicine on time. 允许 (“allow”) does not fit a calendar.

items.text:
A：电影七点开始，现在六点半，我们还（ ）吗？
B：打车过去的话，应该没问题。
items.explain: 来得及 (“there is still time”) is the question about whether they can make the film: half an hour to a seven o'clock start. 打车…没问题 answers it.

items.text:
A：外面雨很大，你（ ）要记得带伞。
B：知道了，妈妈。
items.explain: 千万 (“absolutely, be sure to”) strengthens a request or warning: “千万要记得带伞” because the rain is heavy. 到底 (“on earth”) is used in questions.

items.text:
A：你说这件事（ ）是谁的错？
B：我也不清楚，还是先别讨论了吧。
items.explain: 到底 (“on earth, exactly”) pushes for a real answer in a question: “这件事到底是谁的错？”. 从来 (“never before”) does not fit a question like this.

items.text:
A：这家饭馆的菜怎么样？
B：味道（ ）不错，就是价格有点儿贵。
items.explain: 确实 (“indeed, truly”) confirms a good point before the turn “就是价格有点儿贵”: the taste really is good. It sits before the adjective 不错.

items.text:
A：这个周末我们去爬山吧，（ ）再叫上小张。
B：好啊，我来给他打电话。
items.explain: 另外 (“in addition”) adds a further suggestion to the hiking plan: “我们去爬山吧，另外再叫上小张”. 千万 (“be sure to”) would make it a warning.

items.text: 这里是医院，（ ）大声说话。
items.explain: 禁止 (“to forbid”) states a ban: in a hospital, “禁止大声说话”. It is stronger than a request and takes a verb phrase as its object.

items.text: 我家（ ）公司很近，走路只要十分钟。
items.explain: 距离 (“to be at a distance from”) as a verb: “我家距离公司很近” means home is close to the office. The 走路十分钟 detail supports it.

items.text: 为了（ ）用水，我们洗完手要马上关好水龙头。
items.explain: 节约 (“to save, economize”) collocates with 用水: “节约用水” means saving water; “关好水龙头” is how to do it.

items.text: 他把这件事的经过说得很（ ），大家都听明白了。
items.explain: 详细 (“detailed”) follows 说得 as a degree complement: he explained it in detail, so “大家都听明白了”. 害羞 (“shy”) is about feelings, not explaining.

items.text: 虽然已经学了三年，但他说中文的时候（ ）有点儿紧张。
items.explain: 仍然 (“still”) fits “虽然…但…仍然”: despite three years of study, he is still a bit nervous. It is an adverb before 有点儿紧张.

items.text:
A：今天的会我（ ）来不及参加了，我还在机场。
B：没关系，我会把会上讨论的内容发给你。
items.explain: 恐怕 (“I'm afraid, probably”) softens bad news: I'm afraid I can't make it, because I'm still at the airport. It precedes the verb phrase 来不及.

items.text:
A：你的汉语说得真（ ）！学了多长时间了？
B：谢谢，我学了两年了。
items.explain: 流利 (“fluent”) describes speech: “汉语说得真流利” is praise, and the follow-up asks how long they've studied. It follows 得 as a complement.

items.text:
A：你要去图书馆？（ ）帮我还一本书吧。
B：好的，书在哪儿？
items.explain: 顺便 (“while you're at it”): since you are going to the library anyway, return one book for me on the way. 究竟 (“on earth”) is for questions.

items.text:
A：为了我们的成功，（ ）！
B：干杯！祝大家工作顺利！
items.explain: 干杯 (“cheers”) is a verb used to propose a toast; the reply repeats “干杯！”. It follows the toast “为了我们的成功”.

items.text:
A：真（ ），我来晚了，路上太堵了。
B：没事，我们也刚到。
items.explain: 抱歉 (“sorry”) is an adjective used in apology: “真抱歉，我来晚了”. The reply “没事” (no problem) confirms it is an apology.

items.text: 这个工作的（ ）很大，一百多个人只要两个。
items.explain: 竞争 (“competition”) goes with 很大: “竞争很大” means fierce competition, shown by one hundred people for two places. 基础 (“foundation”) does not fit.

items.text: 学外语的时候，一定要把（ ）打好。
items.explain: 基础 (“foundation”) forms the collocation “打好基础”, to lay a solid foundation, in language study. 把 puts it before the verb 打好.

items.text: 今天的风特别（ ），我的帽子都被吹跑了。
items.explain: 厉害 (“fierce, severe”) describes wind: “风特别厉害”, so strong that it blew off my hat. 竞争 is a noun and cannot follow 特别 here.

items.text: 每个人的想法不一样，我们应该互相（ ）。
items.explain: 尊重 (“to respect”) is the verb for “everyone thinks differently”: 互相尊重 means respect each other. 及时 (“in time”) is an adverb and cannot follow 互相 this way.

items.text: 遇到问题要（ ）解决，别等到最后。
items.explain: 及时 (“promptly, in time”) is an adverb before 解决, contrasted with “别等到最后” (don't wait until the end). 厉害 does not fit.

items.text:
A：这家饭馆的菜怎么样？
B：很好吃，而且价格也不贵，很（ ）去。
items.explain: 值得 (“worth”) forms “值得去”, worth going to: the food is tasty and cheap. 其实 (“actually”) would not fit before a verb with 很.

items.text:
A：我觉得他有点儿不好相处。
B：（ ）他人很好，只是不太爱说话。
items.explain: 其实 (“actually, in fact”) corrects the earlier impression: he seems hard to get along with, but in fact he is nice. 正好 (“just right”) does not contrast.

items.text:
A：你想吃什么？我请客。
B：（ ），我什么都吃。
items.explain: 随便 (“whatever you like”) is the reply to a host asking what you want: “随便，我什么都吃”. It states no preference.

items.text:
A：我想出国读书，但是我爸妈都（ ）。
B：你可以和他们好好谈谈。
items.explain: 反对 (“to oppose”) fits “我想出国读书，但是我爸妈都反对”: 但是 signals an obstacle, and the reply suggests talking it over.

items.text:
A：你来得（ ），我们刚准备出发。
B：太好了，那我跟你们一起去。
items.explain: 正好 (“just in time, just right”) fits “你来得正好”: you arrived exactly as we were about to leave. The pattern is 来得 + 正好.

items.text: 这次比赛输了，大家都很（ ）。
items.explain: 失望 (“disappointed”) is the feeling after losing a match (“输了”). It follows 很 as a degree adverb. 困难 (“difficulty”) is a noun.

items.text: 我们的老师对学生要求非常（ ），作业写错一个字也要改。
items.explain: 严格 (“strict”) fits “要求非常严格”; the example of correcting even one wrong character shows how strict. 对…要求 + 严格 is the pattern.

items.text: 遇到（ ）的时候，不要放弃，要想办法解决。
items.explain: 困难 (“difficulty”) is a noun before 的时候: “遇到困难的时候” means when you meet difficulties; 遇到困难 is a fixed collocation. 失望 would not fit the next clause.

items.text: 经理（ ）下个月给大家放三天假。
items.explain: 保证 (“to guarantee”) is a verb whose object is a promise: the manager guarantees three days of holiday next month. 原因 (“reason”) is a noun.

items.text: 医生说，他生病的主要（ ）是太累了。
items.explain: 原因 (“reason, cause”) is the noun after “主要”: the main cause of his illness, and “是太累了” gives it. 印象 (“impression”) does not fit.

items.text:
A：这张照片是（ ）为你拍的，送给你。
B：太谢谢你了！
items.explain: 专门 (“specially, for the purpose of”) is an adverb before 为你拍: the photo was taken specially for you. 另外 (“in addition”) would not show purpose.

items.text:
A：昨天的晚会特别有意思，你怎么没来？
B：我加班了，真（ ）！
items.explain: 可惜 (“what a pity”) expresses regret about missing the party because of overtime: “我加班了，真可惜！”. 害怕 (“afraid”) is not regret.

items.text:
A：你（ ）去不去？大家都在等你呢。
B：我去，马上就来。
items.explain: 到底 (“on earth”) in the question “你到底去不去？” presses for an answer, since everyone is waiting. It is used with a question form.

items.text:
A：你为什么不敢开车？
B：我（ ）路上出问题，还是坐地铁吧。
items.explain: 害怕 (“to be afraid”) takes a clause: he is afraid something goes wrong on the road, which explains why he doesn't dare to drive.

items.text:
A：这个周末我们去哪儿玩儿？
B：去海边吧，（ ）我还想去看看我的老同学。
items.explain: 另外 (“in addition, besides”) adds a second reason after 去海边吧: also visit an old classmate. It starts the new clause.

items.text: 因为下大雨，今天的比赛（ ）到明天了。
items.explain: 推迟 (“to postpone”) fits “推迟到明天”: because of the rain the match is delayed until tomorrow. The pattern is 推迟 + 到 + time.

items.text: 工作以后，他慢慢（ ）了很多经验。
items.explain: 积累 (“to accumulate”) forms the fixed collocation “积累经验”: after starting work he slowly gathered experience. 引起 (“to cause”) does not take 经验.

items.text: 看完这部电影，很多人都被（ ）哭了。
items.explain: 感动 (“to move emotionally”) in the passive “被…感动哭了”: many people were moved to tears by the film. 引起 (“cause”) cannot take 哭 this way.

items.text: 刚来北京的时候，她很不（ ）这里的天气。
items.explain: 适应 (“to adapt to”) forms “不适应这里的天气”: not used to the weather here, as she has just arrived in Beijing. 不 negates the verb.

items.text: 他对这次考试很有（ ），觉得自己一定能通过。
items.explain: 信心 (“confidence”) forms “有信心”: he is confident about the exam, as “觉得自己一定能通过” explains. 感动 (“moved”) is a verb and does not fit.

items.text:
A：这次出差（ ）吗？
B：挺好的，客户对我们很满意。
items.explain: 顺利 (“smooth, going well”) is the adjective asked about in “出差顺利吗？”; the reply says it went well. 肯定 (“certain”) does not fit a business trip.

items.text:
A：你看，我的考试得了一百分！
B：太好了，老师（ ）你了吗？
items.explain: 表扬 (“to praise”) is the verb: a full score on the test, so did the teacher praise you? 了 + 吗 asks whether it happened.

items.text:
A：小李（ ）把钥匙忘在公司了，现在进不了门。
B：真没想到他会这么粗心。
items.explain: 竟然 (“unexpectedly”) shows surprise at forgetting the keys; the reply “真没想到他会这么粗心” echoes this. It goes before 把.

items.text:
A：明天会下雨吗？
B：（ ）下不下雨，我们都要去。
items.explain: 不管 (“no matter”) pairs with the choice “下不下雨” and with 都: no matter whether it rains, we will go. 仔细 does not fit.

items.text:
A：你觉得他会来吗？
B：（ ）会，他答应我了。
items.explain: 肯定 (“definitely”) is an adverb before 会: he will definitely come, because “他答应我了” (he promised). 竟然 would express surprise, not certainty.

items.text: 每天晚上吃不完的饭菜都扔了，太（ ）了。
items.explain: 浪费 (“to waste, wasteful”) fits throwing away leftover food every evening: “太浪费了”. 太…了 frames an adjective or verb of this kind.

items.text: 这次比赛，我们班（ ）了第一名。
items.explain: 获得 (“to obtain, win”) takes 第一名 as its object: our class won first place. 超过 (“to exceed”) is about going past a number.

items.text: 他的条件完全（ ）公司的要求。
items.explain: 符合 (“to meet, conform to”) forms “符合要求”: his qualifications fully meet the company's requirements. 获得 would not suit 要求.

items.text: 这个城市的人口已经（ ）了一千万。
items.explain: 超过 (“to exceed”) is used with numbers: the population has gone past ten million. The 了 marks the completed change.

items.text: 老师很有（ ），不管我们问什么问题，他都会回答。
items.explain: 耐心 (“patience”) is the noun after 有: “很有耐心”. The teacher answers every question, which shows patience. 浪费 (“waste”) does not fit.

items.text:
A：这件衣服我穿怎么样？
B：很好看，颜色也很（ ）你。
items.explain: 适合 (“to suit”) takes a person as object: the colour suits you. 相反 (“opposite”) does not suit a compliment.

items.text:
A：从这儿到机场要多长时间？
B：（ ）要一个小时，你早点儿出发吧。
items.explain: 至少 (“at least”) sets a minimum time: the trip to the airport takes at least an hour, so leave early. 尤其 (“especially”) does not set a minimum.

items.text:
A：你喜欢中国菜吗？
B：很喜欢，（ ）是辣的菜。
items.explain: 尤其 (“especially”) picks one member out of what was just mentioned: Chinese food in general, and spicy dishes in particular: “尤其是辣的菜”.

items.text:
A：快点儿走吧，（ ）就赶不上火车了。
B：好，我马上就来。
items.explain: 否则 (“otherwise”) states the bad result if you do not hurry: “快点儿走，否则就赶不上火车了”. It joins an instruction to its consequence.

items.text:
A：（ ）你不知道明天要考试吗？
B：啊？我真的忘了！
items.explain: 难道 (“could it be that”) begins a rhetorical question expecting a yes: “难道你不知道…吗？”. The speaker is surprised, and the 吗 at the end is its sign.

items.text: 现在，用手机付钱在中国已经非常（ ）了。
items.explain: 普遍 (“widespread, common”) fits paying by phone being common in China. The pattern is 非常普遍. 激动 (“excited”) describes people, not a custom.

items.text: 在河边玩儿很（ ），你们一定要小心。
items.explain: 危险 (“dangerous”) is the adjective after 很: playing by the river is dangerous, so be careful. 激动 does not fit.

items.text: 请大家（ ）要求填写这张表格。
items.explain: 按照 (“according to”) takes a noun: “按照要求填写”, fill in the form as required. 任何 (“any”) must precede a noun and is not a preposition.

items.text: 他们俩虽然是兄弟，但是（ ）完全不一样。
items.explain: 性格 (“personality”) is the noun: the brothers have completely different personalities. “虽然…但是” signals the contrast with being brothers.

items.text: 听到自己考上了大学的消息，他（ ）得说不出话来。
items.explain: 激动 (“excited, moved”) goes before the complement 得说不出话来: so excited he couldn't speak, on hearing he got into university.

items.text:
A：这里是图书馆，说话小声点儿，别（ ）别人看书。
B：好的，对不起。
items.explain: 打扰 (“to disturb”) takes 别人 as its object: don't disturb others reading. The setting, a library, signals quiet.

items.text:
A：飞机十点起飞，现在才八点，去机场还（ ）吗？
B：打车四十分钟，没问题。
items.explain: 来得及 (“there is still time”): the flight takes off at ten and it is only eight, so can we still make it? 估计 (“estimate”) does not make a question like this.

items.text:
A：你知道小王什么时候到吗？
B：我（ ）他十点左右能到。
items.explain: 估计 (“to estimate, reckon”) fits a guess about arrival: “我估计他十点左右能到”. 左右 (“about”) supports an approximate time.

items.text:
A：（ ）你帮我把这个箱子搬到楼上，好吗？
B：没问题。
items.explain: 麻烦 (“to trouble someone”) opens a polite request: “麻烦你帮我…，好吗？”. 顺便 would need the speaker to be going there anyway.

items.text:
A：你的新房子装修好了吗？
B：还没有，我（ ）住在朋友家。
items.explain: 暂时 (“temporarily, for the time being”) fits: the new flat is not finished, so I'm living at a friend's place for now.

items.text: 这家酒店为客人（ ）免费的早餐。
items.explain: 提供 (“to provide”) takes 免费的早餐: the hotel provides free breakfast for guests. The pattern is 为 + person + 提供 + thing.

items.text: 他每天早上都（ ）跑步，已经跑了三年了。
items.explain: 坚持 (“to persist”) before 跑步: he keeps running every morning, and “已经跑了三年了” confirms the persistence.

items.text: 这次的活动内容很（ ），有唱歌、跳舞，还有游戏。
items.explain: 丰富 (“rich, varied”) describes content, with singing, dancing and games as examples of variety. The pattern is 内容很丰富.

items.text: 这种药的（ ）不错，我吃了两天就好了。
items.explain: 效果 (“effect”) goes with a medicine: it works well, and I was better in two days. 提供 (“provide”) does not suit this sentence.

items.text: 见到老师的时候，他总是（ ）打招呼。
items.explain: 主动 (“taking the initiative”) before 打招呼: he greets the teacher first, without waiting. 表示 (“to express”) does not fit here.

items.text:
A：你怎么没去看电影？
B：我（ ）想去，后来公司突然让我加班。
items.explain: 本来 (“originally”) sets up a plan that changed: “本来想去，后来…加班”. 后来 (“later”) in the next clause signals the change.

items.text:
A：这件事（ ）是谁做的？
B：我也不知道，我们问问小张吧。
items.explain: 究竟 (“on earth, exactly”) presses a question about who did it: “这件事究竟是谁做的？”. It must appear in a question.

items.text:
A：你觉得这次考试难吗？
B：（ ）很难，很多题我都不会做。
items.explain: 确实 (“indeed, truly”) agrees with the question and strengthens it: the exam really was hard, and many questions he couldn't do.

items.text:
A：（ ）你还不相信我吗？
B：不是不相信，只是有点儿担心。
items.explain: 难道 (“could it be that”) opens a rhetorical question: “难道你还不相信我吗？”. The reply denies the doubt, so it is a challenge, not a real question.

items.text:
A：你昨天不是说要去爬山吗？
B：（ ）下雨了，只好在家休息。
items.explain: 可是 (“but”) contrasts the plan to climb with “下雨了”: you meant to go, but it rained, so I stayed home. 于是 (“so”) would not contrast.

items.text: 他是我们公司最（ ）的员工之一，每年都获奖。
items.explain: 优秀 (“outstanding”) fits 最…的员工之一: one of the best staff, who wins an award every year. It describes a person.

items.text: 我们公司正在（ ）新员工，你有兴趣吗？
items.explain: 招聘 (“to recruit”) takes 新员工 as its object: the company is recruiting new staff, and asks if you are interested.

items.text: 这次旅行的主要（ ）是了解当地的文化。
items.explain: 目的 (“purpose, aim”) is the noun after “主要”: the main aim of the trip is to learn about local culture. 合适 (“suitable”) does not fit.

items.text: 经过三次面试，他终于（ ）了。
items.explain: 通过 (“to pass”) is used for an interview: after three interviews he finally passed. 终于 (“finally”) and 了 mark the result.

items.text: 这双鞋的大小正（ ），我就买它了。
items.explain: 合适 (“suitable, fitting”) in “大小正合适”: the shoe size is just right, so I'll buy them. 正 + adjective means exactly.

items.text:
A：你常常去健身房吗？
B：不常去，（ ）去一两次。
items.explain: 偶尔 (“occasionally”) answers “常常去吗？”: he doesn't go often, only once or twice now and then. 往往 (“often, usually”) is the opposite.

items.text:
A：这个地方的风景（ ）美啊！
B：是啊，我们多照几张照片吧。
items.explain: 多么 (“how, such”) in an exclamation: “风景多么美啊！”. The pattern is 多么 + adjective + 啊. 由于 does not form an exclamation.

items.text:
A：（ ）你已经决定了，我就不再说什么了。
B：谢谢你理解我。
items.explain: 既然 (“since, now that”) refers to something already settled: since you have decided, I won't say more. It pairs with 就.

items.text:
A：你（ ）一个人去国外旅行吗？
B：当然敢，我已经去过好几个国家了。
items.explain: 敢 (“to dare”) is the verb in “你敢一个人去…吗？”, and the answer “当然敢” repeats it. Travelling alone abroad is the thing to dare.

items.text:
A：今天的航班怎么取消了？
B：（ ）天气不好，飞机不能起飞。
items.explain: 由于 (“because of”) gives the reason for the cancelled flight: bad weather, so the plane can't take off. The reason comes first in this pattern.

items.text: 这次活动由小王（ ），有问题可以直接找他。
items.explain: 负责 (“to be in charge of”) in “由小王负责”: Xiao Wang is responsible, so ask him directly. The pattern is 由 + person + 负责.

items.text: 虽然遇到了很多困难，但是他还是（ ）坚持了下去。
items.explain: 继续 (“to continue”) comes before 坚持: despite many difficulties he kept on persisting. 虽然…但是 sets the contrast.

items.text: 今天我（ ）太累了，想早点儿睡觉。
items.explain: 实在 (“really, truly”) is an adverb strengthening 太累了: I'm really too tired, so I want to sleep early. 感觉 is a verb of feeling.

items.text: 这家店每天卖的面包（ ）不多，去晚了就买不到了。
items.explain: 数量 (“quantity”) is the noun: the bread sold daily is not much, so go early. 面包数量不多 means the amount is small.

items.text: 吃完这个药以后，我（ ）好多了。
items.explain: 感觉 (“to feel”) is the verb: after taking the medicine I feel much better. 好多了 shows the result.

items.text:
A：外面雨这么大，公园是去不了了。
B：那我们（ ）在家看电影了。
items.explain: 只好 (“have no choice but to”) follows an impossible plan: the park is out because of rain, so we have to watch a film at home.

items.text:
A：这道题太难了，（ ）老师都不会做。
B：真的吗？那我们去问问别的老师吧。
items.explain: 连 (“even”) forms “连…都”: even the teacher can't do it, which shows how hard the problem is. 都 follows the noun phrase.

items.text:
A：明天的考试很重要，你（ ）别迟到。
B：放心吧，我会早点儿出门的。
items.explain: 千万 (“be sure not to”) strengthens the warning “别迟到”: don't be late for the important exam. The pattern is 千万 + 别 or 要.

items.text:
A：他都说了三遍了，（ ）你还不明白吗？
B：我真的没听懂，你再说一遍吧。
items.explain: 难道 (“could it be that”) forms a rhetorical question ending in 吗: after three explanations, you still don't understand? 究竟 does not suit a yes/no 吗 question.

items.text:
A：小李来了吗？
B：还没有，他（ ）要晚一点儿才能到。
items.explain: 恐怕 (“I'm afraid”) softly predicts bad news: he is not here yet and will probably be late. 要 + 晚一点儿 gives the prediction.

items.text: 为了（ ）浪费，这家饭馆推出了小份的菜。
items.explain: 减少 (“to reduce”) takes 浪费 as its object: to cut waste, the restaurant offers small portions. 所有 (“all”) is not a verb.

items.text: 事实（ ）他的办法是对的。
items.explain: 证明 (“to prove”) fits “事实证明…”: the facts prove his method was right. It is a fixed way to introduce a result.

items.text: 她是学法律（ ）的，毕业以后当了律师。
items.explain: 专业 (“major, field of study”) forms “学法律专业的”: she studied law, and then became a lawyer. 所有 (“all”) does not fit here.

items.text: 手机每天早上七点都会（ ）我起床。
items.explain: 提醒 (“to remind”) takes 我 plus a verb: the phone reminds me to get up at seven every morning. 证明 does not fit.

items.text: 我们班（ ）的同学都参加了这次比赛。
items.explain: 所有 (“all”) goes before a noun with 的: “所有的同学” means every classmate in our class. 专业 and 羡慕 do not fit before 同学.

items.text:
A：你（ ）喜欢哪一件？快点儿决定吧。
B：我也不知道，两件都很好看。
items.explain: 到底 (“on earth”) pushes for a decision in a question: which one do you actually like? “快点儿决定吧” shows the impatience.

items.text:
A：你去商店的时候，（ ）帮我买一个面包。
B：好的，没问题。
items.explain: 顺便 (“while you're at it”): when you go to the shop anyway, buy me a bread too. It marks a small extra errand.

items.text:
A：这个菜真好吃，是你做的吗？
B：是的，我第一次做，没想到（ ）这么成功。
items.explain: 竟然 (“unexpectedly”) goes with “没想到”: it was the first time cooking, yet it came out so well. It marks surprise.

items.text:
A：这次旅行你们要去几个城市？
B：先去北京，（ ）还要去上海和西安。
items.explain: 另外 (“in addition”) adds more places after 先去北京: also Shanghai and Xi'an. 往往 (“often”) would not add items.

items.text:
A：你们结婚十年了，感情还这么好。
B：是啊，我们过得很（ ）。
items.explain: 幸福 (“happy, blessed”) describes married life: after ten years, still close, so “我们过得很幸福”. It follows 很 as an adjective.

items.text: 学校（ ），上课的时候不能用手机。
items.explain: 规定 (“to stipulate”) is the verb of a rule: the school rules that phones can't be used in class. 印象 (“impression”) does not fit.

items.text: 这两件衣服的（ ）只是颜色不一样。
items.explain: 区别 (“difference”) is the noun: the only difference between the two garments is the colour. “只是颜色不一样” states it.

items.text: 他对工作非常（ ），经常主动帮助同事。
items.explain: 积极 (“positive, active”) describes his attitude to work; “经常主动帮助同事” gives the example. 适应 is a verb and does not fit.

items.text: 已经到了晚上十点，办公室里的灯（ ）亮着。
items.explain: 仍然 (“still”) says the lights are still on even though it is ten at night. It is an adverb before 亮着.

items.text: 刚到北方的时候，我很不（ ）这里的天气。
items.explain: 适应 (“to adapt”) forms “不适应天气”: not used to the weather in the north, as the speaker has just arrived. 不 comes before the verb.

items.text:
A：我找了半天钥匙，（ ）在你这儿啊！
B：对不起，昨天忘了还给你了。
items.explain: 原来 (“so it turns out”) marks a discovery: after a long search, the keys were with you. 本来 (“originally”) describes an old plan, not a discovery.

items.text:
A：你（ ）一个人去国外旅游吗？
B：当然敢，我已经去过好几次了。
items.explain: 敢 (“to dare”) in “你敢一个人去…吗？”; the reply “当然敢” repeats it. The sentence asks about courage to travel alone.

items.text:
A：这家饭馆的菜怎么样？
B：（ ）不错，就是有点儿贵。
items.explain: 确实 (“really, indeed”) agrees that the food is good before the turn “就是有点儿贵”. 原来 (“turns out”) would imply a discovery.

items.text:
A：听说那场演出特别精彩。
B：真（ ），我没买到票。
items.explain: 可惜 (“what a pity”) is regret: the show was great but I couldn't get a ticket. It follows 真 as an adjective.

items.text:
A：（ ）你把窗户打开，好吗？
B：好的。
items.explain: 麻烦 (“to trouble”) opens a polite request: “麻烦你把窗户打开，好吗？”. The sentence has no discovery or contrast, so 本来 does not fit.

items.text: 请大家按照（ ）排队上车。
items.explain: 顺序 (“order, sequence”) forms “按照顺序排队”: queue up to board in order. 按照 needs a noun as its object.

items.text: 这个问题我们明天开会再（ ）吧。
items.explain: 讨论 (“to discuss”) is the verb with the problem as object: we will talk it over at tomorrow's meeting. 再 + verb means do it later.

items.text: 因为他工作认真，经理在会上（ ）了他。
items.explain: 表扬 (“to praise”) fits: because he works carefully, the manager praised him at the meeting. 了 marks the finished action.

items.text: 我们公司的员工人数已经（ ）了去年的两倍。
items.explain: 超过 (“to exceed”) goes with a number: staff numbers have gone past twice last year's figure. 增加 would not take 去年的两倍 as naturally.

items.text: 最近来这个城市旅游的人不断（ ）。
items.explain: 增加 (“to increase”) is used without an object here: visitors keep rising, with 不断 (“continuously”) before it. 超过 needs an object.

items.text:
A：你每天都（ ）吃药吗？
B：是的，医生让我一天吃三次。
items.explain: 按时 (“on time”) is an adverb before 吃药; the reply “一天吃三次” gives the fixed schedule. 无论 (“no matter”) starts a clause instead.

items.text:
A：我（ ）你已经回家了，怎么还在公司？
B：还有一点儿工作没做完。
items.explain: 以为 (“to assume (wrongly)”) fits “我以为你已经回家了，怎么还在公司？”: the speaker's belief proved false. 对于 does not take a clause like this.

items.text:
A：这个周末大家都去吗？
B：（ ）小张，大家都去。他要出差。
items.explain: 除了 (“except”) pairs with 都: everyone is going except Xiao Zhang, and the reason (“他要出差”) explains why he is excluded.

items.text:
A：她的中文怎么样？
B：非常好，（ ）比中国人说得还标准。
items.explain: 甚至 (“even”) raises the degree: her Chinese is so good that it is even more standard than a Chinese person's. It comes before 比.

items.text:
A：你真的要去吗？
B：是的，（ ）多难，我都要去试一试。
items.explain: 无论 (“no matter”) pairs with 多难 and 都: no matter how hard it is, I'll try. It introduces an unconditional clause.

items.text: 老师（ ）大家明天上午九点在学校门口见面。
items.explain: 通知 (“to notify”) takes 大家 and then the content: the teacher informs everyone to meet at nine tomorrow. 经验 is a noun and cannot take this structure.

items.text: 这场足球比赛非常（ ），大家都看得很激动。
items.explain: 精彩 (“wonderful, brilliant”) describes a match, which explains why everyone was excited: “看得很激动”. 危险 (“dangerous”) does not fit.

items.text: 我们班有三十个学生，（ ）有十个是留学生。
items.explain: 其中 (“among them”) refers back to the thirty students: ten of them are international students. It stands as the subject of 有.

items.text: 他有很多年的工作（ ），所以很快就解决了问题。
items.explain: 经验 (“experience”) forms “工作经验”: many years of work experience, so he solved the problem quickly. 安静 (“quiet”) does not fit.

items.text: 天太黑了，一个人在山上走很（ ）。
items.explain: 危险 (“dangerous”) describes walking alone on a mountain at night because “天太黑了”. It follows 很 as an adjective.

items.text:
A：这是我（ ）为你做的蛋糕。
B：太谢谢你了！
items.explain: 专门 (“specially”) is an adverb before 为你做: I made the cake specially for you. 故意 (“deliberately”) implies intent to harm and does not fit a gift.

items.text:
A：你怎么把我的书弄坏了？
B：对不起，我不是（ ）的。
items.explain: 故意 (“deliberately”) forms “不是故意的”: I didn't do it on purpose, an apology for breaking the book. The pattern is 是…的.

items.text:
A：你喝过这种茶吗？
B：（ ）没喝过，这是第一次。
items.explain: 从来 (“never before, ever”) goes with a negative: “从来没喝过” means never drunk it, confirmed by “这是第一次”.

items.text:
A：今天的飞机怎么晚了？
B：（ ）天气不好，飞机晚了两个小时。
items.explain: 由于 (“because of”) gives the reason: bad weather, so the plane was two hours late. The reason noun phrase comes straight after it.

items.text:
A：你为什么这么晚才下班？
B：明天要交报告，我（ ）加班。
items.explain: 不得不 (“have no choice but to”) fits: the report is due tomorrow, so I have to work overtime. It is followed by the verb 加班.
